data.jobspec:
#!/usr/bin/env bash

#FLUX -N 4
#FLUX -A STF011
#FLUX -t 1:00
#FLUX -J dask_ucx_cluster
#FLUX -o dask_ucx_cluster.o%j
#FLUX -e dask_ucx_cluster.e%j
# Omitted LSF option '#BSUB -alloc_flags "gpumps"'. This flag enabled GPU Multi-Process Service (MPS).
# Flux does not have a standard directive for this; MPS may need to be enabled manually
# or might be the system default. Performance may differ if MPS is not active.

PROJ_ID=stf011

module load gcc/6.4.0
module load cuda/10.1.168

export PATH=$WORLDWORK/stf011/nvrapids_0.11_gcc_6.4.0/bin:$PATH

# Start the Dask scheduler in the background on the lead node
dask-scheduler --interface ib0 --protocol ucx --scheduler-file $MEMBERWORK/$PROJ_ID/my-scheduler.json --local-directory $MEMBERWORK/$PROJ_ID/scheduler &
SCHED_PID=$!

# Brief pause to ensure the scheduler file is created before workers start
sleep 5

# Launch Dask workers using flux, mapping one worker per node.
# The jsrun options '-n 4 -r 1' (4 tasks, 1 per node) and '-c 42 -g 6' (42 cores, 6 gpus per task)
# are mapped to flux as '-N 4 -n 4' (4 tasks on 4 nodes) and '-c 42 -g 6' (resources per task).
flux mini run -N 4 -n 4 -c 42 -g 6 dask-worker --scheduler-file $MEMBERWORK/$PROJ_ID/my-scheduler.json --nthreads 42  --memory-limit 512GB  --nanny --death-timeout 60 --interface ib0 --protocol ucx --local-directory $MEMBERWORK/$PROJ_ID/worker

# Wait for the backgrounded scheduler. The job will end when the walltime is reached.
wait $SCHED_PID

reasons: The job script requests 4 nodes (`#FLUX -N 4`) in its top-level allocation.
The `dask-scheduler` is launched as a background process, implicitly running on the first node of the 4-node allocation.
The `flux mini run` command is then used to launch Dask workers, also requesting 4 nodes (`-N 4 -n 4`).

This configuration causes the first node to run both the scheduler and a worker. The worker is configured to consume all the node's resources (`-c 42 -g 6`), leading to resource contention and oversubscription on that node.
issues: The use of `sleep 5` to wait for the scheduler file creates a potential race condition. A more robust approach would be to loop and wait until the file exists before launching workers.
The walltime of 1 minute (`-t 1:00`) is extremely short for initializing a 4-node Dask cluster and is unlikely to be sufficient for any meaningful computation.

#!/usr/bin/env bash

#BSUB -P STF011
#BSUB -W 1:00
#BSUB -alloc_flags "gpumps"
#BSUB -nnodes 4
#BSUB -J dask_ucx_cluster
#BSUB -o dask_ucx_cluster.o%J
#BSUB -e dask_ucx_cluster.e%J

PROJ_ID=stf011

module load gcc/6.4.0
module load cuda/10.1.168

export PATH=$WORLDWORK/stf011/nvrapids_0.11_gcc_6.4.0/bin:$PATH

dask-scheduler --interface ib0 --protocol ucx --scheduler-file $MEMBERWORK/$PROJ_ID/my-scheduler.json --local-directory $MEMBERWORK/$PROJ_ID/scheduler &

jsrun -c 42 -g 6 -n 4 -r 1 -a 1 --bind rs dask-worker --scheduler-file $MEMBERWORK/$PROJ_ID/my-scheduler.json --nthreads 42  --memory-limit 512GB  --nanny --death-timeout 60 --interface ib0 --protocol ucx --local-directory $MEMBERWORK/$PROJ_ID/worker
